concentrations are expected to reach levels that pose a health risk.

level ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing
difficulties for children, older adults, as well as persons with
respiratory problems.

regularly scheduled work day you are urged to consider
telecommuting, carpooling, or utilizing public transit. Avoid
excessive idling and do not top off when refueling motor vehicles.
The use of gasoline-powered lawn equipment should be reduced or
postponed until late in the day.

For more information visit the St. Louis Clean Air Partnership at
http://cleanair-stlouis.com/

For current Air Quality Index (AQI) values visit
https://www.airnow.gov/

bring scattered thunderstorms this afternoon and evening with
outflow wind gusts up to 50 mph and little rainfall. As the low
moves into southeastern Oregon late tonight and southwestern
Idaho on Friday, scattered thunderstorms will develop again,
especially on the Idaho side.

The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Fire Weather
Watch for winds and low relative humidities, which is in effect
from after midnight tonight through Friday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Idaho, Fire Weather Zones 423 Owyhee
Mountains, 424 Western Twin Falls BLM and 426 Southern
Highlands.

* TIMING...From late tonight through Friday evening.

* WINDS...Northwest 5 to 15 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...34 to 46 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...65 to 73 degrees.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are possible. Listen for later forecasts and possible Red Flag
Warnings.

properties.description:
ESFLOT

Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms are possible starting
late Friday night and continuing into Monday across southern
Wisconsin, northern Illinois, and part of northwestern Indiana. High
moisture content in the atmosphere will lead to torrential downpours
where thunderstorms are most frequent, leading to the potential for
several inches of rain on a widespread basis.

The favored area for several rounds of showers and thunderstorms
Friday night through Monday will be near and north of Interstate 80
where several inches of rain have fallen in the past 24 hours. The
intersection of increasingly saturated soils and repeated downpours
may lead to areas of flooding and rises in river levels, including
along the Rock, Fox, DuPage, and Illinois rivers.

This outlook means that elevated water levels and potential impacts
are possible, but not yet certain. Persons should closely monitor
forecasts including the possibility of flood watches, warnings, and
advisories.

Additional statements or outlooks may be issued by tomorrow morning.
